sources.entry: Semantic Versioning Will Not Save You

summary.title: Semantic Versioning Will Not Save You
summary.one_liner: Semantic Versioning cannot prevent breakage or make upgrades safe, so users should pin exact versions, test thoroughly, and treat every update as potentially breaking.
keywords: why pin major version is bad
takeaways: Hyrum's Law means any observable behavior can be depended on, so SemVer cannot guarantee non-breaking minor or patch updates.
Pinning a major version only postpones breakage and can leave applications without security updates once the package moves to a new major version.
Users should pin exact versions of dependencies and transitive dependencies, run good tests, and regularly update with fixes.
Blocking a single broken version (e.g. Flask!=1.1.2) is preferable to pinning a major version (e.g. Flask<2), which should be temporary.
Maintainers may use SemVer optionally, but 0ver projects and major-version pinning create burden and version conflicts.
summary.summary: The author argues that Semantic Versioning cannot protect users from breakage, using Hyrum's Law and examples from the cryptography Rust build-system controversy. He explains how pinning major versions leads to missed security updates, transitive version conflicts for downstream users, and ZeroVer maintainer burnout. The practical advice is for users to pin exact versions, keep test coverage high, update regularly, and block only specific broken versions or temporarily block a major version while migrating.
